# NOTES

## BOOK 1: OUT OF THE BLUE (Bertrand W. Sinclair)

**Cast:** Rock Holloway (narrator focus; long-limbed Texan ranger, keen eyes, educated back East, not a degree; rides sorrel horse **Sangre**; black pony carries bed; gray Stetson; .45 Colt; reata). Uncle Bill Sayre (Fort Worth Trinity Bank president, ~60, Southern dialect "yo'", "fo'", "sho'", "No'th"; cattle owner, distrusts co-executor). Marcus Proud, Abel Stewart (other bank partners). Rock's mother; sister Cecilia "Cissy" (17, marrying a Brett, son of Brett who runs the B X near El Paso). Rock's father (dead; "Steve" not stated here). Duffy brothers: Joe (noisy, harmless), Elmer (trail boss, Seventy Seven; tenacious, moody), Ed (tough), Mark (huge, bully, "Big Duffy"). Dave Snell (dead Maltese Cross owner; Trinity River, west fork). Buck Walters (Maltese Cross range boss, co-executor; young, ambitious, flashy dresser, poker, women, agate-gray eyes). Alice Snell (21, heiress, tawny/yellow hair, black brows, blue-purple eyes). Snell son (16). Al Kerr (Texan cattleman, Waco; tiny ~5'4", gnomelike, blue eyes; Capital K, Judith Basin on Arrow Creek, P.O. Lewistown). Dave Wells (Texan boss of Steering Wheel/"Wagon Wheel" on Old Man River, Canada; tall, thin, drawly). Billy Gore; red-headed deputy foreman. Nona Parke (~21, TL ranch on Marias; dark hair, deep-gray eyes, scarlet lips, throaty voice, imperious, independent). Betty Parke (3-4, blonde, blue eyes, green calico, rag doll; calls Rock "Doc"). Doc Martin (dead TL rider, look-alike of Rock, shot in chest). Charlie Shaw (~20, blue-eyed TL rider, Doc's friend). Mary Vieux (16, half-breed girl, cook/nurse). Joe Stack and Bill Hurley (hired gunmen, Buck's pets; Hurley shot Doc). Two Maltese Cross riders (dead in ambush). Joe Bishop (TL/round-up rider).

**Ch I. A Retaining Fee.** Spring, Fort Worth. Rock visits Trinity Bank ("Holy" chalked on door). Sayre: Duffy brothers, Elmer runs Seventy Seven herd north. Rock to Montana with Seventy Seven; plans to quit at destination. Dave Snell died; estate of ~30,000 cattle (Maltese Cross) moved to Montana (~10,000 there, rest Texas, "$300,000 worth"). Estate run as going concern till boy is 25; income paid to each child; executors Sayre and Buck Walters. Sayre distrusts Walters. Sayre hires Rock as private watcher: "keep cases on Maltese Cross." Gives $500 gold in canvas bag, $60/month. "Retaining fee" metaphor. Marias River, P.O. Fort Benton; Maltese Cross on lower Marias near Missouri. Rock to be in Montana about September. Rock rides out, talks to sorrel Sangre near Trinity.

**Ch II. In the Odeon.** Clark's Ford, Nebraska river crossing (sandy, quicksand; Ben Clark's name). Camp: general store, blacksmith, saloon/dance hall the **Odeon** (name painted in white). July evening. Rock meets Al Kerr at a poker table. Mark Duffy enters drunk; drinks a stranger's whisky; "Make room for a man." Lifts Kerr onto bar, shakes him, orders "Buy drinks or dance." Duffy fires shot into floor at Kerr's feet. Rock steps between with Colt: "You've gone far enough with this, Duffy. Don't be a damn fool." Duffy draws; Rock fires, kills Mark. Rock tosses Duffy's gun to Kerr. Kerr's six riders escort out. Kerr invites Rock to Judith Basin. Rock was camped 9 miles north; Seventy Seven camp; two months' wages due. Duffys clannish; blood feud fear.

**Ch III. The Steering Wheel.** Rock leaves Seventy Seven. Three days out meets Maltese Cross herd (camp by nameless creek). Joins northbound Steering Wheel herd (1,200 cattle, 8 men, bound to Fort MacLeod, Old Man River, Canada). Crosses Yellowstone, Missouri (where Chief Joseph forded), Bear Paws right, Sweet Grass Hills left. Wintering on Old Man; Dave Wells runs ranch; hay cut with mower; Billy Gore. Wells sends 4 riders away in April; Rock stays till May. Wells's 5-man horse gather with 40 horses, returns ridden out; pays 4 men gold; they leave south via Butte, Silver Bow Junction. Cattle: fresh-burned Steering Wheel, unbranded "doggies"/longhorns with Hereford touch; Rock suspects rustling. Rock parts 5 days later under Sweet Grass Hills, heads to Fort Benton. Quote: "Here we comes, and there we goes, / And where we'll stop nobody knows."

**Ch IV. A Dead Double.** Halfway Milk River–Marias: US cavalry (Fort Assiniboine 80 miles east) mule packing, 5 days, $5/day, Rock earns $25. Drops into Marias valley. TL ranch: pine log house, L-shaped, stable with two saddled horses, one with blood-stained saddle. Nona sits with face in hands; Betty says "'Lo 'Doc'." Nona shocked: thinks Rock is Doc. Dead man: Doc Martin, blue-rimmed chest wound, still warm, half hour dead. Rock identical to him. Doc had separated to look at cattle around bend; heard one shot; Doc rode back dying. Nona's father died after horse fell on him (back injury, nearly a year). Mother died at Betty's birth. Nearest neighbors: Maltese Cross 7 miles below, Seventy Seven 7 miles above. Nona suspects Elmer Duffy. Rock gives name: Rock Holloway, Texas. Supper; Rock fetches water from spring by willows; Rock washes dishes; Betty asleep on his knee. Rock sleeps by stable under stars, Orion's belt.

**Ch V. Wrapped in Canvas.** Dawn. Nona bathes body, dresses in blue serge. Burial at sunrise under giant cottonwood, picket fence, two graves (mother, father) plus Doc's. Body wrapped in heavy canvas; no lumber for coffin. Nona kneels and prays.

**Ch VI. Very Adroit Rock.** Nona offers job: $50/month (Doc was $40 ~ "ten dollars" difference). Rules: no sentiment. Rock milks cows (no). Nona: about 800 TL cattle; round-up with Maltese Cross; father drove 3 herds from Pecos, lost most; 4 yrs ago ~9,000 cattle, 12 riders; first winter brutal, round-up gathered <500. Doc was jealous, quarrelled with Elmer Duffy; Doc threatened Elmer, told him never to set foot on ranch. Elmer rides up; Rock says "Hello, Duffy"; Duffy thinks he's Doc, says "Hellow, Doc." Rock: "Up the river somebody took a pot shot at me. Nona heard it." Duffy: "I'm no bushwhacker... When I shoot at you, I'll be lookin' you in the eye." Rock poses as Doc to take pressure off Nona; Duffy agrees to let it go. Nona: "Adroit." Rock explains to Nona why he poses as Doc; she says "Suit yourself." Nona: "Rope that sorrel for me and that chunky bay for yourself... catch me that black pony." Ride down Marias with Nona and Betty (cushion on saddle; Betty calls him Doc); half-breed nurse at Vieux's down river. Nona's directions: draw north, Lonesome Prairie, cattle with TL left rib brand.

**Ch VII. Mariners.** Rock rides the draw; counts TL and Maltese Cross cattle; odd 77. Meets round-up at White Springs: Charlie Shaw (blue eyes, white teeth) on Parke horse; Joe Bishop; Alice Snell (tawny hair, black brows, pansy-blue eyes, dimple, green corduroy split skirt, carved saddle with silver). Alice: "You haven't wandered around our way for over two weeks." Rock eats with Maltese Cross crew. Buck Walters (agate-gray eyes, well-dressed, tall; ~30) stares: "Hello, Martin." Rock: "You seem kinda surprised to see me." Rock reflects: Walters is administrator, Snell estate. Alice invites Nona to ride down. Rock tells Nona about Mark Duffy death. Nona: Elmer hated Doc, Alice's long-suit is attention, Buck "detests" Buck? (Nona says Alice detests Buck). Nona: "Alice... ornamental but quite useless." Rock compliments Nona; she says "Don't be silly." Rock weeds lettuce. Week of rides; Nona's hidden little herds, "miser" feeling; Rock uneasy. Rock dislikes Buck. Return: Charlie in camp, talking with Nona on porch.

**Ch VIII. Getting Down to Cases.** Charlie reports calf count: ~70–80 fewer calves than expected. Charlie: rumor Rock rustling with **Burris boys** behind **the Goosebill** (odd hill, halfway Marias–Fort Benton). Charlie: Buck will "get" Doc over Alice. Rock asks about riding rig; Rock shows Charlie Doc's locked room: saddle with blood stain, bridle, black Angora-faced chaps, silver-inlaid spurs, worn boots, belt with .45 cartridges, black-handled Colt, felt hat, canvas war bag. Charlie: Doc "was a white man." Charlie says Doc was crazy about Alice; Alice said she'd can Buck if her dad hadn't made him administrator. Buck's eyes burn at Doc's name. Charlie: Buck has hard men in crew: two "killers" who stay at home ranch with horses. Charlie tells Rock: "I'd rather have [Nona] for a boss." Nona assigns Rock: go to Fort Benton, hire two haying men (200 tons hay).

**Ch IX. Ordered South.** Rock at Fort Benton (oldest settlement; Northwest Fur Co.; Grand Union Hotel; ferry; Bear Paws 50 miles east; Judith Basin freight). Bar at Grand Union: Walters and Dave Wells. Wells: "I'd know your hide on a fence in hell"; "you're Rock Holloway, darn you!" Walters claims Rock is "Doc Martin." Rock hires two men. Night, Walters confronts Rock on street: "This country ain't healthy for you no more, Martin... go South." Rock refuses, insults; Walters: "I will have you put away." Walters: "my friend Dave Wells will kill you." Walters: "I will shut your mouth for good, inside of forty-eight hours." Rock lies down, sleeps.

**Ch X. Thirty Angry Men.** Next day (~24 hours later). Alice gallops to TL: "Buck Walters and Elmer Duffy, with all the boys, are coming to hang you!" "They say you're stealing cattle." 30 riders, rifles. Rock with carbine in doorway; Nona and Alice on porch. Walters: "We want him... dead or alive. He is a thief." Nona: "That... is a lie." Rock: "I am not Doc Martin." Nona confirms Doc dead, shot ten days ago. Charlie inside with two guns. Duffy: "If you ain't Doc Martin, there's only one other man you could be." Rock names Rock Holloway; points to sorrel JB horse, black Bleeding Heart horse. Duffy: "You're Rock Holloway." Walters blames Burrises: "We've cleaned out his partners." Walters taunts Duffy about Mark. Walters: "I hope you don't hold grudges." Alice: "Doc Martin never stole anything in his life... You were afraid of him... I hate you." Walters: "So long, boys!" rides off.

**Ch XI. Riders on a Rise.** Alice in tears; Nona comforts. Rock thinks about Alice (pansy-blue eyes). Nona & Rock talk: Elmer's brooding; "You steal hearts." Rock teases; "I'll be your boss." Rock tells Nona of new Montana county election (superior judge, sheriff, treasurer, clerk, commissioners) in a month. Nona: "time we were getting civilized." Rock agrees to hay 2–3 weeks. Alice to stay at TL with Nona. Charlie: Burris cleanup was last night by Buck's pets. Charlie: "Doc's dead. Let his troubles stay buried." Rock & Charlie ride to gather 7–8 work horses near Maltese Cross springs; two riders on rise behind. Ambush in ravine (service-berry brush): shot kills Rock's horse; Rock grazed on scalp. Rock wounds/kills first shooter, chases second (sorrel rider on Maltese Cross horse); shoots sorrel's horse down; captures rider; hog-ties with hair macarte. Captured man's sorrel bears Maltese Cross. Other man dead, horse saddled, Maltese Cross brand.

**Ch XII. Stack Decides to Talk.** Captive: **Joe Stack** (other = **Bill Hurley**). Rock's Holloway kin: father Steve Holloway (US marshal at Abilene); Tom Holloway ("Long Tom," Texas ranger captain); Ben Holloway (Ragged H, Milk River, cousin). Stack's foot burned by fire; Rock's spurred foot on knee. Stack confesses: Buck offered $500 (to Stack & Hurley) to kill Rock; Hurley shot Doc. Stack says Buck is "goin' North for a spell, with a hand-picked crew." Rock releases Stack on the Maltese Cross horse and gives blanket & grub; keeps other horse; Stack walks out in plain sight; heads south. Rock rides home.

**Ch XIII. On the Warpath.** Nona dresses scalp wound with carbolic acid and court-plaster. Rock tells her nothing; "a horse fell and cut my head." Charlie reports Buck took a wagon, half crew, saddle horses, and left after the mornings' session; hard pills gone. Rock: "Birds of a feather." Rock tells Charlie of "hidden branding pens with chute, tucked in the Sweet Grass." Doc had said Buck wanted to grab Alice and outfit; Doc had "put a bug in Buck's ear." Rock leaves at dawn; Nona cooks bacon, packs lunch. Rock kisses Nona by Sangre; rides off. "Kill or cure." Rock crosses Missouri, ferry, Billings (Northern Pacific), Judith Basin to Kerr's Capital K (Buffalo Creek). Kerr: Sayre loaned him $20,000; Kerr knew Dave Snell. Kerr offers men and horses.

**Ch XIV. Hot on the Trail.** Billings telegraph office (long telegram to Sayre; tips operator $10; N.P. Hotel). Sayre's reply: "Act on your own judgment. Will back any action you take. Suspected this. Coming north, first train. Sayre." Rock hired buggy & driver; drove 110 miles to Kerr ranch in 17 hours. Next dawn Rock rides north with dozen Capital K men, chuck wagon, 100 horses; ferried Missouri; Marias above Nona's upper fence. Charlie Shaw joins at camp: he went alone to Sweet Grass, found corrals; Buck and six pets camped on creek 5 miles from corrals, five riders with pack outfits and 40 horses joined from North. Charlie declines Rock's invitation to supper; goes home (Nona with Alice and Mary Vieux).

**Ch XV. Popping Guns.** Sweet Grass Hills: Gold Butte, West Butte, East Butte. Rock camps wagon on East Butte. Scout with Charlie through lodgepole gulch; lookout on bank shoots Charlie (falls into wild cherry, wounded). Corrals: dumbbell-shape, branding fire, cattle rebranded from Maltese Cross to Steering Wheel. Buck and Dave Wells seen working. Rock flees on horse; pursued by ~13 riders; horse shot down; Capital K riders arrive firing. Buck charges on coal-black white-faced horse; Rock shoots Buck at 20 yards. Riderless black horse falls on Rock; flying hoof strikes him. Blackout; sees Nona's face.

**Ch XVI. "Certainly Not Sad."** Maltese Cross herd with Capital K horses. Rock in house with Uncle Bill Sayre (~"bloated bankers"); Rock explains: Dave Wells, Steering Wheel; Stack talk; paper marks showing Maltese Cross → Steering Wheel. Sayre: Buck borrowed $25,000 a year ago as co-administrator, bought 1,200 head in Panhandle. Sayre offers Rock management of Maltese Cross; Rock says "I'll tell you tomorrow." Sayre: calves: "brand a hundred for her." Buggy to TL; Sayre drives. Elmer Duffy at TL kitchen pleading to marry Nona. Rock: Buck "stealing wholesale." Elmer: "Well, by heck!" Duffy shakes Rock's hand; leaves. Charlie shot, wagoned to Benton. Rock & Nona; she says "I like you a heap." She weeps; "there are two times when every woman cries... I'm certainly not sad!"

## BOOK 2: LORD STRANLEIGH ABROAD (Robert Barr)

Ward, Locke & Co., 1913. Frontispiece: "'Why did you wish to murder me?'" (p. 189). Chapters: I Lord Stranleigh All at Sea; II An Automobile Ride; III The God in the Car; IV The Mad Miss Maturin; V In Search of Game; VI The Bunk House Prisoner; VII The End of the Contest.

**Cast:** Lord Stranleigh (Edmund Trevelyan; Evelyn Trevelyan; of Wychwood; rich, shy, indolent, dislikes publicity, excellent tailor, good athlete, never allowed to be troubled; uses aliases Trevelyan, Henry Johnson, Henry Johnson the chauffeur). Ponderby (valet, Londoner, disapproves of America, blushes, once disobeys master). Hon. John Hazel ("Jack"; ex-Camperdown Club, expelled, cardsharp, ex-friend). Ship's doctor (unnamed). Purser (unnamed). Trevelyan-kin woman (name not given; "Miss Trevelyan"; later Mrs. Branksome Poole). Charles Branksome Poole (alias; ex-chauffeur, forger, gambler, blackmailer; wanted in NY for blackmailing millionaire **Erasmus Blank**). Wentworth Parkes (ex-valet of Duke of Rattleborough; forged letter; swindler). Duke of Rattleborough (Camperdown). J. E. Sterling (young Detroit engineer, Woodbridge Street). John L. Banks (Ice Trust attorney, NY). Stanley Armstrong (Montana rancher, ex-mining engineer; Bleachers). Mrs. Armstrong. Miss Armstrong (Dr., Lausanne-trained; lectures in an Eastern medical college). Jim Dean (guide's leader; bunk-house leader; ear shot). Peter (ranch man). Silas A. Ricketts (Bleachers lawyer, $5 hour; holds Armstrong note $5,000). Sheriff (Bleachers, popular). Asa Perkins (Boston, owner of house). Challis: James "Jim" Challis (engineer, grist mill, Fulmer's; gone smash). Gertrude Challis (née Anson). Stanmore Anson (Swedish-descent yeoman, stubborn; Anson's Mill; Trust; Langdon, Bliss & Co.). Mrs. Anson. Edward "Ned" Trenton (Philadelphia coal/railways; ex-"Ned"). Mrs. Vanderveldt ("Sis"; married ex-minister to Italy). Constance Maturin (~young, forests/factories; co-owner Powerville with John L. Boscombe; "mad" model city). John L. Boscombe (millionaire, opposes Maturin).

**Ch I. Lord Stranleigh All at Sea.** Southampton → Cherbourg → Queenstown → New York on largest Atlantic liner. Stranleigh (Edmund Trevelyan) boards; Ponderby sent to suite. Ship doctor: promoted; Stranleigh gets seat at his table. Hazel in steerage (3rd class) with "William Jones" ticket; Stranleigh gets him cabin **4390**, swaps purser for £5 notes. Ponderby packs Hazel a costume from Stranleigh's 37 suits; Hazel adopts name "John Hazel." Hazel promises no cards all the way. Lunch with doctor. Evening: pretty young woman (Trevelyan-kin) says purse stolen (£ in pocket); Stranleigh gives two £50 notes, fifty plus fifty. Later Poole enters Stranleigh's rooms uninvited: "Lord Stranleigh, I presume?" Demands £100 "given to my wife"; reads note numbers; Stranleigh confirms. Poole: wife is Mrs. Branksome Poole. Stranleigh orders Ponderby to bar Poole. Ponderby throws Poole into corridor. Wife in Ponderby's room, tells story: met Charles Branksome, chauffeur, father's motor tour America 5 yrs ago; secret marriage before justice of peace; father refused pay; died 2 yrs later. Poole: liar, thief, forger, brute; used her as decoy; wanted by NY police for blackmailing Erasmus Blank. Stranleigh arranges she gets divorce; she leaves. Hazel plays poker with Poole, catches cheating ("You have dealt yourself..."), chief officer and captain; Poole detained; wireless to NY. Wife collects money; two £50 notes in her possession.

**Ch II. An Automobile Ride.** Stranleigh in New York as Trevelyan; newspapers swarm; changes hotels; moves to Canada. Wentworth Parkes, with Duke of Rattleborough letter, pitches Sterling Motor Company (Detroit; $100,000 share). Stranleigh drives with Parkes. Stranleigh cables Duke: reply: "Letter a forgery. Parkes was my valet for three years... RATTLEBOROUGH." Stranleigh and Ponderby flee NY via Boston, St. John NB; Ponderby sells steamship tickets. Stranleigh registers as **Henry Johnson** in Detroit hotel near river. Ponderby homesick for Thames. Chauffeur hired; drives to Woodbridge Street; J. E. Sterling's shop: runabout, "Repairs promptly executed." Sterling: engineer, option; earlier option to an Englishman who took a car and vanished. Safety pegs: centre stops engine/brakes; right-hand peg turns right; left turns left. Stranleigh takes option: $500 deposit (five $100 bills) for one week. Parkes sees them through window; Parkes becomes chauffeur for test drive. Drive along Canadian shore toward Lake St. Clair. Parkes demands $100,000 at road bank; Stranleigh: "I say 'No!'" Stranleigh wrestles Parkes off wheel, pegs halt car, Stranleigh hurls Parkes into shallow river. Stranleigh returns; Parkes to Sterling; Sterling to pay $500 + Stranleigh adds $500 for Parkes to sign no-molest. Capitalize company $100k–$500k.

**Ch III. The God in the Car.** Stranleigh and Ponderby at Altonville (Indian summer; furnished house for Ponderby; Ponderby's $15,000 at Altonville bank; Burford/Lenthall/butler precedent). Stranleigh drives; drives Challises: Mrs. Challis's sprained ankle; young couple at lake. Jim Challis (engineer, grist mill at Fulmer's; mill shut down). Challis's story: worked for Langdon, Bliss & Co. (advisers); sent to Anson's mill (stone factory, 3 generations; overshot waterwheels; wasteful). Report; Anson raged, fired Challis; Challis married Gertrude Anson (father's permission given later). Father's letter to daughter disowning? Anson cut off. Mill up for auction: Seventeenth of November (bankruptcy court). Anson's house also sale. Stranleigh and Challis drive to Anson's; Stranleigh tells Mrs. Anson he is ambassador from daughter; Mrs. Anson gives key via housekeeper; trunks stored at Asa Perkins's house (Stranleigh rents). Stanmore Anson meets Stranleigh; asks about G.K.R. Trust; dispute over manager (Anson insists; Stranleigh insists Challis). Anson reverses: "I did you a great injustice." Anson accepts payment for mill. Gertrude enters: "Shall we throw our differences on that scrap-heap?" Anson embraces her.

**Ch IV. The Mad Miss Maturin.** Ned Trenton hosts Stranleigh (Pennsylvania estate; Philadelphia). Sister Mrs. Vanderveldt (married ex-minister to Italy). Constance Maturin (friend; dams and lakes; father's company legally limited; Boscombe as co-owner). Ned's coal and railway wealth; lost a suit; dynamited a dam earlier; Miss Maturin's dam at Powerville. Water-wardens with telephones in each lake cottage; automobile road through forest. Stranleigh meets Mrs. Vanderveldt and Maturin. Mrs. Vanderveldt says Maturin went to England to meet Stranleigh seeking capital. Maturin's six-cylinder runabout; drive through forest lakes; Maturin reveals Powerville model city; Boscombe obstructs; Stranleigh buys Powerville stock (fails: Boscombe refuses); Boscombe visits Stranleigh: Maturin "stark mad." Holiday entertainment at Powerville heights: brass band, free refreshments; dam overflows; "Great heavens!"; Maturin: "Look at that wave!" Dam bursts; valley town and mills destroyed. Boscombe: "This is murder!" Stranleigh: "Whoever is responsible for the weakness of that dam should be hanged!"

**Ch V. In Search of Game.** Stranleigh in NY, University Club; attorney John L. Banks (Ice Trust) advises ranch: Stanley Armstrong (mining engineer, set limit £100,000). Letter of introduction written by Banks. Stranleigh travels by train to Bleachers, hires guide, horse, pack mules. Ambush at edge of Armstrong's ranch: shot in left shoulder by Jim Dean; guide and escort abandon packs; Stranleigh raises arms; shouts parley. Mrs. Armstrong at door; Armstrong "in Chicago." Miss Armstrong dresses wound; bullet through shoulder; sling; tells him rest. Miss Armstrong's background: Lausanne, Thun (Thunerhof and Falken), cooking school at Thun, professor of medicine at Eastern college; ambition American Madame Curie. Jim Dean whistle; Jim says he fired "to nip" Stranleigh, took him for sheriff; "I'm the peaceablest man on earth." Miss Armstrong: sheriff seizes property; ranch mortgaged to Ricketts for $5,000; father's partners; silver mine; father walking home from Chicago. Stranleigh: will pay debt, offers $2,000 + $3,000 (= $5,500; "two thousand dollars" cash offered by Miss Armstrong, "three thousand" by Stranleigh). Ricketts refuses. Stranleigh notes Miss Armstrong's exact money. Miss Armstrong and Stranleigh at dinner; trout; cigars.

**Ch VI. The Bunk House Prisoner.** Stranleigh recovers; visits silver mine tunnel (dynamite stored at end; cataract). Jim and three men stop him: keep off west of imaginary line; Stranleigh's rock returned. Jim: "Mr. Dean... partner." Stranleigh: Jim's men distrust city people; "rattlesnake season" lawyers; Ricketts visited with mining engineer. Stranleigh tells Miss Armstrong he will find father via detective; she distrusts men. Stranleigh rides to Bleachers (Ricketts office, $5 hour; Ricketts reads Armstrong's letter; Armstrong wrote from Chicago). Stranleigh telegraphs NY detective (Burns) and Pinkerton (Chicago) for Armstrong: $100 reward, "EDMUND STRANLEIGH, White's Hotel, Bleachers." Telegraph operator: Ricketts paid him $1 to report telegrams; Stranleigh sends fake Pinkerton message; sends cypher telegram to NY agent for $20,000 currency. Stranleigh returns to ranch; Jim and five men seize him at clearing at dusk. Stranleigh held in bunk house (stone fortress; door guarded; slits at gables). Men: "We are not gaolers." Jim demands Stranleigh lend Armstrong money; Stranleigh refuses. Stranleigh gives Havana cigars. Stranleigh lectures on work. Chimney fire-soot, idea of escape.

**Ch VII. The End of the Contest.** Night, Stranleigh climbs chimney while guard Jim sleeps; creeps to farmhouse (barefoot, soot-covered); takes magazine rifle, cartridges, bread, ham, tobacco, candles, bedclothes. Builds barricade across mine mouth with stones intersticed with dynamite. Jim steps out at dawn; Stranleigh shoots Jim's left ear; then shoots out "S" in door panel (door punctured). Stranleigh demands parley; threatens siege, offers explosion ultimatum: "the person who sets off that dynamite is a murderer." Armistice: men agree to stay, not break out until auction. Jim visits Miss Armstrong; ear treated ("sting of a bee"). Miss Armstrong notices bloody handkerchief with crest and monogram (Stranleigh's family crest). Stranleigh teaches Miss Armstrong fly fishing. Next morning Stranleigh goes to bunk house, offers $50 each for six men as bodyguard at auction, pays $300 (six $50 bills); conditions: no drinking, no shooting until command. Stranleigh meets Armstrong on road; Armstrong broke, Chicago rascals; they agree to buy ranch with $500 transferred. Express package of $20,000 collected; Armstrong identifies. Auction at Agricultural Hall, Bleachers: Ricketts (two strangers beside him) bids $3,000; Stranleigh $5,000; Ricketts $6,000; Stranleigh $10,000; Ricketts $11,000; Stranleigh $15,000; Ricketts $16,000; Stranleigh $17,000 ("Going! Gone!"). Ricketts demands postponement; sheriff keeps sale. Stranleigh pays $17,000 cash. Stranleigh gives Miss Armstrong documents as payment of medical bill (also Jim's); $10–12k to Armstrong's daughter; Stranleigh leaves for London. Miss Armstrong: "Good-bye to you, Lord Stranleigh of Wychwood." Stranleigh: she read NY paper about "Earl Stranleigh of Wychwood" plus handkerchief monogram. END.

**Other:** Transcriber's note: Book 2 story from Ward, Lock & Co., 1913; Book 2 publisher ads list other Ward Lock titles (not story content).
